tools.name: Kim
tools.summary: Catalog and explicit installer for Kim tools
tools.description: Lists Kim tools and installs, updates or removes them only when you ask. Never installs anything by itself.

tools.name: Subak
tools.summary: Persistent Windows-first terminal with a separate Host and Clients
tools.description: Sessions live in a per-user background Host and survive closing every window. Headless CLI, optional native GUI, Claude Code status. Not released yet.

tools.name: Noeul
tools.summary: Screenshot and pin tool: F1 captures a region, double-click pins it on the desktop
tools.description: A small native screenshot utility in the spirit of Snipaste. F1 starts a region capture, a double-click inside the selection pins it as a floating window, and F3 pins the clipboard image. It stays in the notification area while you use it and uses no keyboard hook. Not released yet.
features: F1 starts a region capture; a double-click inside the selection pins it to the desktop
F3 pins the image on the clipboard as a floating window
Copy (Ctrl+C) or save (Ctrl+S) a selection or a pin; Esc cancels
Planned: annotation, color picker, capture history, multi-monitor and high-DPI support
Every shortcut can be changed, turned off or reset

entry_points.summary: Starts Noeul in the notification area; F1 and F3 work while it runs
Captures a screen region to a file without opening a window (needs an unlocked desktop)
Reports whether Noeul runs, its pins and its shortcut registrations
Lists Noeul's shortcuts with their state (the hotkey contract's commands)
Describes Noeul's commands for agents and `kim tools describe`
Optional local MCP adapter with allowlisted capture and pin actions

links.title: Noeul design and Snipaste parity plan (Step 48)

permissions.detail: F1 and F3 are registered system-wide only while Noeul runs (RegisterHotKey, no keyboard hook)
Reads the screen only when you start a capture; nothing leaves your computer
Reads an image from the clipboard for F3 and writes the captures you copy
Starts when you sign in only if you turn that on in its settings

tools.name: Ddalgak
tools.summary: Automation engine: one key press runs the remaps, text, launches and macros you define
tools.description: Ddalgak turns triggers you choose into actions: remap keys, type text, open programs or websites, move the mouse, switch modes and run multi-step macros. Rules are made in a visual editor or with a headless CLI. Its keyboard hook exists only while you have the engine turned on, and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Esc always turns it off. Not released yet.
features: Rules: a trigger (key, chord or sequence) runs one action or ordered steps
Actions: remap keys, type Unicode text, open programs and websites, move and click the mouse
Planned: modes, app-specific rules, profiles, macro recording and a safe test playground
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Esc always turns the engine off and releases held keys
Visual rule editor, plus a headless CLI for scripts and agents

entry_points.summary: Starts Ddalgak with its tray icon and rule editor; the engine stays off until you turn it on
Lists your rules without opening a window
Simulates rules in the test playground; injects no input
Pauses every rule of the running engine
Lists Ddalgak's own shortcuts and its rule triggers (the hotkey contract's commands)
Optional local MCP adapter: read-only inspection, explicitly permissioned changes

actions.title: Turn the automation engine on or off
Emergency off: remove the hook and release held keys

permissions.detail: A low-level keyboard hook exists only while you have the engine on; it acts on your rule triggers only and records no keystrokes
Types text and sends keys or mouse input only when one of your rules says so
Opens programs or websites only when one of your rules says so
Moves, activates or closes windows only when one of your rules says so
Reads or writes the clipboard only when one of your rules says so
Its own shortcuts (engine on or off, pause, editor) are registered system-wide while it runs, once you bind them
Starts when you sign in only if you turn that on
